correctness.rationale: Three internally disjoint s-t rails and the terminal neighborhood fix optimum size 3. Every minimum cut hits each rail once. Explicit bypasses force adjacent-column inequalities and endpoint placements if bypass rows exist. A left/right vertex partition proves sufficiency. The resulting three-coordinate state lists give all four TS/TJ graph classes for all n>=3,w>=4 and interior r. Two standalone checkers passed direct BFS enumeration for 56 parameter choices and separate coordinate graph checks for 1232 choices. No computational extrapolation is used for the infinite domain.

value.rationale: A complete infinite-parameter classification of minimum network cutset replacements identifies a sharp terminal-depth transition: outer-adjacent minima support two movable three-state TS components, but adding an intervening row freezes all slide moves. The n=3 exceptional TJ prism/C4 class isolates the difference between physically local and unrestricted relocation. This is a natural structural boundary in optimum cutset maintenance, rather than a miscellaneous small-graph table.
